newsitem.title: GERMANY: German opposition say U.S. N-tests undermine pact.
newsitem.headline: German opposition say U.S. N-tests undermine pact.

text.p: Germany's opposition Social Democrats (SPD) and environmentalist Greens criticised the United States on Thursday for conducting nuclear tests in the Nevada desert, which they said undermined the spirit of a recent test ban.

"The announced sub-critical nuclear tests by the U.S. are formally permitted, but politically damaging," said SPD deputy Gernot Erler, who heads the German parliament's disarmament and weapons control committee.

The experiments, announced on Wednesday, were designed to test weapons materials without triggering the kind of nuclear chain reaction prohibited by the international Comprehensive Test Ban Treaty signed last year.

"The critics of this treaty in countries on the threshold of having nuclear weapons will feel justified. Washington is unnecessarily endangering the joint Western goal of an effective non-proliferation regime," Erler said.
Greens defence spokeswoman Angelika Beer agreed, saying non-aligned countries like India would feel their distrust of the pact was justified.

"With this agreement, the owners of nuclear weapons secured the possibility of being able to continue tests which allow them to further develop nuclear weapons. At the same time they have ruled out tests for less developed states," Beer said.
